subject.title: fix(tasks): skip session pruning when cron-state read fails (#110935)

question: When persisted cron state cannot be read, should `tasks maintenance --apply` continue non-session maintenance while skipping only session-registry pruning, or abort the entire maintenance pass?
rationale: The linked bug report identifies both behaviors as plausible and the PR selects one without maintainer discussion; this is an error-path product policy rather than a mechanical correctness choice.

options.title: Keep maintenance localized
options.body: Continue unrelated task/task-flow maintenance, but leave the session registry untouched whenever cron state cannot be read.

options.title: Abort the whole maintenance pass
options.body: Treat unavailable cron state as a global maintenance precondition and return before any maintenance mutations.

recommendation.title: Keep maintenance localized
recommendation.body: Continue unrelated task/task-flow maintenance, but leave the session registry untouched whenever cron state cannot be read.

likelyOwner.reason: Repository guidance connects this area to cron, making Tyler the best available routing candidate despite limited history provenance.
